_comment: Chapter 05 (workload identity federation and managed identities): every call the NpiFederation module makes, with the least-privileged Microsoft Graph permission, Azure role or Active Directory right from the Learn page for that call, read on October 30, 2026. Same schema as calls.json; kept in its own file so chapters written in parallel don't collide. 'federation' only reads (GET and Get-AD*), plus the token exchange test, which is fixture-only and never leaves the machine. 'federation-apply' is the separate, delegated write path, run only with an approved plan hash and -Apply. tests/NpiFederation.Tests.ps1 fails when a task's declaration isn't exactly the union of its calls.

adRights: Delegated right to disable accounts in the account's OU

calls.note: Reads appId, passwordCredentials and keyCredentials ($select) so the token exchange test has the client ID and the parallel run knows the legacy secret.
The List page names Application.Read.All; the Get page names Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy (Chapter 01's research gap 4). The apply re-reads before each create.
Confirms a system-assigned managed identity's service principal exists (servicePrincipalType ManagedIdentity) and gives its client ID for the sign-in evidence.

Service principal and managed identity sign-ins, with clientCredentialType and federatedCredentialId, are on beta only; Learn needs an explicit signInEventTypes filter and a P1 or P2 license. Delegated, the person needs Reports Reader or another listed role.

Learn's how-to names Managed Identity Operator or Managed Identity Contributor for reading a user-assigned identity; Reader holds */read and nothing else (research gaps, row 45). A 404 means the identity doesn't exist yet.
Records a managed identity's Azure role assignments ($filter=assignedTo('{objectId}')) in its conversion record. Changing them is Chapter 07's work, not this chapter's.
The legacy account's Enabled and LastLogonDate during the parallel run; the apply re-reads Enabled before the disable. LastLogonDate is a lead, not a fact (Chapter 01's research gap 3).

The client credentials request with a federated credential, sent only to the fake token endpoint in this module. The code refuses to send it anywhere else: a real exchange runs inside the workload, with the workload's own token (Lab 2).

Delegated Application.ReadWrite.All is the only delegated permission Learn lists; the application permission Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy reaches only apps the caller owns. The write path is a person's delegated session with Cloud Application Administrator, or the app's owner.
Learn: creating a user-assigned managed identity needs Managed Identity Contributor. The precheck refuses a PUT on an identity that already exists, so the PUT never updates one.

Learn's trust page names Contributor or Owner; the Managed Identity Contributor built-in role holds federatedIdentityCredentials/write (research gaps, row 45). Sent one at a time per identity: concurrent creates under one identity fail with 409.

calls.adRight: Delegated right to disable accounts in the account's OU
calls.note: Disables the legacy AD account after a clean 30-day parallel run and the application owner's approval. Never deletes (Chapter 02's research gap 15 for the right).
